_about: The ElevenLabs voices a voiceover may be read in, and the only place a voice id for one is kept (his own clone's id is also in krish-clone's registry, which wins; scripts/velib/voice_bank.py refuses a bank whose krish entry disagrees with it). Krish, 2026-11-17: "for all voiceovers and carousels, I want there to either be an audio track over the carousel, or, if it's a voiceover, then I want Eleven Labs voices used to do the voiceovers. I always want to be given a few options in my control center. We should have some stock voices approved in Eleven Labs and, obviously, my own Krish remix voice too as an option on the control center Content Board. voiceovers would have light approved epidemic audio behind the voice." Every voice id was read from ElevenLabs (creative_list_voices, 2026-11-17), never typed from memory. A stock voice is proposed until his press on the Content Board approves it for the bank; only an approved voice is generated (ve voice clone --voice), and the board offers proposed ones marked as proposed so he can hear them. preview_url is ElevenLabs' own free preview clip (no credits spent); the board plays it through GET /api/board/sign-offs?voice=<id>. The words of a sample are never his script: a preview is ElevenLabs' own line.
ruling: Krish, 2026-11-17 (typed in a Claude session): for all voiceovers, ElevenLabs voices, a few options on the Content Board, some approved stock voices and his own Krish Remix voice; voiceovers have light approved Epidemic audio behind the voice; carousels carry an approved audio track

voices.name: Krish Remix
voices.line: His own ElevenLabs voice: "more of a posh london accent with an aussie twang" (its ElevenLabs description).
voices.why: His own voice, the one krish-clone's registry approves (krish-voice-elevenlabs, 15 Nov 2026).

voices.name: Clyde
voices.line: British, middle-aged; power with nuance and humour (ElevenLabs library, professional).
voices.why: The nearest stock voice to his own register: a British narrator who can land a dry line, so a short read in it still sounds like the channel.

voices.name: Jackson
voices.line: American, middle-aged; a confident, credible narrator (ElevenLabs library, professional).
voices.why: A plain, trusted American read for the follow.the.money numbers stories, where the audience is mostly US business owners.

voices.name: Nichalia Schwartz
voices.line: American, 20s to 30s; friendly, bright and clear, made for explainers (ElevenLabs library, professional).
voices.why: A warm explainer voice for the good-news and how-it-works shorts, and a contrast to his own so a week's off days do not all sound alike.

voices.name: Allison
voices.line: British; smooth, elegant and engaging, made for narration and YouTube (ElevenLabs library, professional).
voices.why: A calm British read for the under.the.hood explainers, where a slower, even voice helps a listener follow a mechanism heard once.
